title.narrative: FSDZ Kvinnor & ungdomar i finansiell inkludering WIN 2
FSDZ Women & Youth in Financial Inclusion WIN 2

description.narrative: The WIN 2 programme will contribute to systemic and lasting change, particularly benefiting poor women, youth, and the disabled, through a market systems development approach to financial inclusion and addressing of financial barriers to real sector engagement. The three key work areas are: 1) digitization for financial inclusion, with the aim of reducing transaction costs and increasing market information flows in terms of time and money for poor women, youth, people with disabilities, and their households; 2) financial education, with the aim of improving life conditions of poor women, youth, people with disabilities and their households through improved financial capabilities, leading to improved access to income opportunities, social welfare, basic health and education services; and 3) women and youth savings groups, with the aim of creating agency for women, youth and people with disabilities to improve sustainable income flows, access social services for them and their families, voice opinion and take leadership, as well as enabling increased financial inclusion.

The WIN 2 programme is implemented by Financial Sector Deepening Zambia and is based on lessons learned from the WIN project (June 2016 - February 2020). The time frame for the WIN 2 programme is 2020 to 2025, and the overall budget is SEK 40 million.
The WIN 2 programme will promote greater financial inclusion and capabilities for women, youth, people with disabilities, and their households. The three key work areas are: 1) digitization for financial inclusion; 2) financial education; and 3) women and youth savings groups.
Financial Sector Deepening Zambia will implement this programme together with the Government of Zambia and a number of civil society and private sector partners. Some of the funds will be forwarded to some of these partners.

WIN 2-programmet implementeras av Financial Sector Deepening Zambia och bygger på lärdomar från WIN-projektet (juni 2016 - februari 2020). Tidsramen för WIN 2-programmet är 2020 till 2025 och den totala budgeten är 40 miljoner SEK.
WIN 2-programmet kommer att främja ökad finansiell inkludering och kapacitet för kvinnor, ungdomar, personer med funktionsnedsättning och deras hushåll. De tre viktigaste arbetsområdena är: 1) digitalisering för finansiell integration; 2) finansiell utbildning; och 3) kvinnor och ungdomsbesparingsgrupper.
Financial Sector Deepening Zambia kommer att genomföra detta program tillsammans med Zambias regering och ett antal civilsamhällets organisationer och privata partner. En del av medlen kommer att vidarebefordras till några av dessa partner.

Key Projects Achievements
National Financial Education Curriculum: The National Financial Education Supplementary Curriculum (NFESC) was launched in July 2022 and integrated into the grades 812 curricula. A total of 10,000 supplementary financial literature books were distributed to 100 schools in all ten (10) provinces of Zambia. Teachers reported behavioural changes in students, including savings and microenterprise activities.
Savings Groups (SGs): A total of 71 SGs were formed, including 38 youth groups, 19 womens groups, and four community groups. These groups mobilised ZMW 248,500 in loans with a 99.9% repayment rate. Financial literacy training reached 1,752 individuals (70% female), with 81% reporting improved emergency preparedness and business stability.
Disability Inclusion: Cheshire Homes supported 47 SGs for caregivers of children with disabilities, benefiting 980 caregivers (85% female). Additionally, financial education clubs in 27 schools empowered children with disabilities, enhancing household financial resilience. Innovation Lab Successes: Impact Hub trained 3,364 TEVET students in financial literacy, while Barefeet Theatre used theatre to educate 796 participants (57% female, 12% with disabilities) on financial topics.
Contributions to Systemic Change
Policy Influence: The integration of National Financial Education Supplementary Curriculum (NFESC) into Zambias national curriculum marked a milestone in institutionalising financial literacy. Advocacy efforts also influenced disability-inclusive policies. Gender Equity: Couples savings groups improved joint decision-making, with 93.75% of participants reporting shifts in gender norms. Womens agency increased, with 68.75% challenging biases and accessing low-interest loans for businesses
WIN LABS
The WIN 2 programme established an Innovation Lab where new ideas were developed, tested, refined, and piloted before full-fledged implementation. Successful pilots included: 1. Financial Education Through Theatre implemented by Barefeet. The aim was to promote financial inclusion through the formation of SGs among persons with physical disabilities, and vulnerable young persons and women using theatre for development. 499 participants (204 males, 295 females; 97 with disabilities were reached across Lusaka, Kaoma, and Livingstone. 2. Financial Education and Savings Groups for People with Disabilities by Cheshire Homes. The objectives were to Improve financial literacy and economic empowerment for children with disabilities and their caregivers. The project reached 980 caregivers (834 females) and 514 children with disabilities. The project also formed 47 SGs and 47 Financial Education Clubs in 27 schools.
